title: From the Start
subtitle: Day by day: what happened, what I was thinking, what I did, and which goals or values it touched.

entries.title: Day one: restart, not perfect conditions
entries.story: Restarted The Secret of Secrets. I could not find the Kindle and nearly let that become the reason not to read. I used the phone app instead, read the prologue and then finished chapter 1. I also put the 6pm weekday work-app ban back in place, with no work apps at weekends.
goals: Read at least one chapter a day
No work apps after 6pm on weekdays
entries.avoidance: Missing Kindle and the phone not feeling the same nearly became a reason to put reading off.
entries.response: Used the phone app and read anyway.

entries.title: Action before motivation
entries.story: Read chapter 2. Tidied the bedroom and put clothes away so I was no longer stepping over them. Completed the Raylo SKU setup that had been hanging around. Also collected Elphaba's ashes from the crematorium.
goals: Put clothes away and tidy bedroom
entries.response: Started the job and completed it.

entries.title: The allotment was worse in my head
entries.story: Read chapter 3. Sorted the outdoor plants and started the indoor plants. Went to the allotment for the first time that year just to see what state it was in. It was not as bad as I expected and that gave me confidence to go back.
entries.avoidance: The allotment had been built up into a much bigger job in my head.
entries.response: Changed the goal from 'fix it' to 'go and look'.

entries.title: Section one, not the whole allotment
entries.story: Went back to the allotment and cleared section one, spending about an hour there. Read chapter 4 and listened to chapter 3 on audio, which seemed to help concentration. Bought two large tomato plants and visited Ingham's nursery. Brought the bins in.
entries.response: Kept the allotment broken into sections instead of treating it as one huge job.

entries.title: A lot got closed out
entries.story: Read chapters 5 and 6. Changed the bed, cleared allotment section two and sent Marley Bear's birthday card. The carried-over jobs did not get dropped just because they missed their original day.
goals: Send Marley Bear his birthday card
entries.avoidance: The bed change had been carried over from the weekend.
entries.response: Finished it rather than abandoning it.

entries.title: Kirsty said the progress was huge
entries.story: Met with Kirsty and talked her through the goal-setting grid. She liked it, agreed with the direction and said the avoidance summary showed huge progress. The Amazon return was added as an ongoing task, but it was genuinely blocked because the Post Office was waiting for labels.
goals: Complete Amazon return when labels are available
entries.avoidance: Amazon return was blocked, not avoidance.
entries.response: Kept blocked tasks separate from things I was actually avoiding.

entries.title: Presence instead of more homework
entries.story: Kirsty's homework became a small set of flash-card ideas: carrot not stick, being present with people, enjoying food and finding the treasure in ordinary life. The point was practice during normal life, not creating another huge worksheet.
entries.avoidance: Risk of turning therapy into another list of jobs.

entries.title: Mindfulness week
entries.story: Kirsty's new ask was to try the Chocolate Meditation, Mindfulness of Breath and Body, and the 3-Minute Breathing Space. The aim was not to empty the mind or do it perfectly, but to notice where attention goes and bring it back.
goals: Try Mindfulness of Breath and Body
entries.avoidance: No need to turn mindfulness into another perfection test.
entries.response: Treat the exercises as experiments and notice what happens.

entries.title: Chapter 13
entries.story: Reached chapter 13 of The Secret of Secrets. The reading goal had gone from a restart task into an ongoing habit.

entries.title: More babies to look after
entries.story: Went to Ingham's, my favourite garden centre up the road, and picked up dwarf beans, a couple of chillies and a kiwi plant. The dwarf beans came home looking healthy and ready to grow. More babies to look after.
goals: Look after the new dwarf beans, chillies and kiwi plant
entries.avoidance: None. This was choosing to spend time on something I enjoy.
entries.response: Made room for the gardening hobby and brought home something new to nurture.

entries.title: Chapter 15, Amazon return done, Blackpool ahead
entries.story: Chapters 1-14 are complete and chapter 15 is in progress. Took the Amazon returns back, closing a task that had been waiting on labels. Also talked about really looking forward to Blackpool with Mum and Dad next week, with the tower, high tea and a drag cabaret planned.
entries.response: Closed the Amazon return and kept reading moving.

entries.title: About five weeks in: a new rhythm
entries.story: Looking at the app and the journey so far felt genuinely positive. Only about five weeks into actively working on this, I can see that I have started to build a new rhythm rather than just completing isolated tasks. Reading, acting on avoidance, making room for family and things to look forward to, and keeping the therapy work practical are beginning to feel more like part of normal life.
goals: Keep life connected to my values
entries.avoidance: The important thing now is not to turn the new rhythm into another perfection test.
entries.response: Notice the change, keep doing the small things, and allow imperfect days without treating them as failure.

entries.title: Dante and Amara: something huge to look forward to
entries.story: One of the most important life events in this period has been choosing our new kittens, Dante and Amara. They are only four weeks old now and come home on 24 October. We visit them every two weeks, and Christine sends photo and video updates every few days in between. This is a big source of excitement and something very real to look forward to over the next two months.
goals: Visit Dante and Amara every two weeks
Welcome Dante and Amara home on 24 October
entries.avoidance: None. This is about connection, anticipation and enjoying something good as it develops.
entries.response: Make room to enjoy the visits and updates rather than rushing past the anticipation.

entries.title: Office day and plenty to keep me busy
entries.story: In the office all day with lots of meetings and a stressful Apple product launch. It was a full-on work day.
entries.avoidance: Nothing specific reported during the work day.
entries.response: Got through the busy day and then switched away from work.

entries.title: Date night after a stressful day
entries.story: After the stressful Apple launch work day, I went for date night at Pizza Express with my lovely darling Jason. Instead of letting work take the whole day, the evening became time together and a chance to switch off.
goals: Make time for Jason and connection
entries.avoidance: No avoidance. The important bit was not allowing a stressful work day to swallow the evening as well.
entries.response: Went out for date night and made space for us after work.

entries.title: A really good session with Kirsty
entries.story: Had a great session with Kirsty and showed her Darren's Compass, the app we have built together to keep the diary, therapy work and progress in one place as it grows. She was impressed with it and with how clearly it shows the progress I am making. We talked through the week and also touched on whether some of my attention and concentration patterns could fit with ADHD or being on the spectrum. Kirsty cannot diagnose this, so it is not being treated as a diagnosis, but she can keep those patterns in mind as part of our work. She also gave me some Happiness flash cards to work on, which I will share later so we can capture the exact task properly.
goals: Keep using Darren's Compass as a living record of progress
Share the new Happiness flash cards and complete the agreed task
entries.avoidance: No new avoidance issue identified in the session.
entries.response: Used the session to review real progress and agreed to keep the new homework simple until the exact cards are shared.

entries.title: A customer meal that was genuinely enjoyable
entries.story: Had the customer meal at IBAI yesterday and it was amazing. I took Gavin with me and he loved it too. It was a work event, but also a genuinely enjoyable shared experience rather than just another obligation in the diary.
goals: Make room for enjoyable experiences alongside work
Notice when work includes something genuinely good
entries.response: Let myself enjoy the meal and share the experience with Gavin.

entries.title: A London day to look forward to
entries.story: Really looking forward to our day in London today. First a hair and beard trim, then into town for some shopping and food before watching Abigail's Party in the West End tonight. I might treat us to the oyster bar at Selfridges and dim sum in Chinatown before the play. It feels like a proper day out together, with time to enjoy ourselves rather than rush through it.
goals: Enjoy the day rather than turn it into a checklist
Make time for Jason and shared experiences
Be present for the food, shopping and theatre
entries.avoidance: None. This is about anticipation, connection and making room for enjoyment.
entries.response: Let myself look forward to it and treat the day as something to experience, not something to get through.
